name: Mariglia
description: Mariglia is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from Sardinia, Italy, particularly popular in the North around Sassari, Olbia, and Nuoro. Known as 'Bridge Sardo' (Sardinian Bridge) for its strategic depth, it belongs to the Manille family where the Seven is the highest and most valuable card. The game allows open communication between partners, making it unique among trick-taking games.

overview.description: Mariglia is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from Sardinia, Italy, particularly popular in the North around Sassari, Olbia, and Nuoro. Known as 'Bridge Sardo' (Sardinian Bridge) for its strategic depth, it belongs to the Manille family where the Seven is the highest and most valuable card. history.origins: A Sardinian variant of the Manille family of games, sharing etymology with Manille, Manillen, Malilla, and similar European games where a specific card (the Seven) holds special value.
timeline: Traditional: Developed in Northern Sardinia, particularly Sassari, Olbia, and Nuoro
Nickname: Known as 'Bridge Sardo' due to strategic partnership cooperation
Present: Remains the most popular card game in Northern Sardinia
history.cultural: Played in Sardinian social clubs, cafes, and family gatherings. The open communication between partners is a distinctive social feature.
history.evolution: The name 'Mariglia' clearly shares etymology with Manille/Manillen/Malilla - all games where the Seven (or Ten in some variants) is the highest card.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other. Deal and play are anticlockwise.
setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck of the French-suited Genoese pattern. Ranking: 7 (Mariglia) > Ace > King > Jack > Queen > 6 > 5 > 4 > 3 > 2. Note: Jack ranks higher than Queen (as in Portugal and Southern Italy).
setup.dealing: First dealer chosen by drawing cards (lowest deals). Turn to deal passes to the right. Dealer shuffles, player to left cuts (minimum 5 cards each portion). Deal anticlockwise in packets of 5 cards (two rounds), 10 cards each. Bottom card (dealer's last card) indicates trumps (il trionfo) and is placed face up.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach the target score (35 or 45 game points).
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads to first trick. Each trick has four cards. Won by highest card of led suit, or highest trump if any trumps played.
keyRules: Follow suit if able; if void and opponent is winning the trick, must trump and beat if possible.
Ten tricks per hand; winner of each trick leads to the next. Card points: 7=5, A=4, K=3, J=2, Q=1; each trick adds 1 point.
Team with more than 35 card points scores the difference as game points. First team to reach agreed target (35 or 45) wins the game.
Trump is determined by the dealer's bottom card (il trionfo); dealer's team scores it immediately if it is a counting card.

strategy.basic: The Seven (Mariglia) is the most powerful card - 5 points and unbeatable in its suit. Guard your Sevens and Aces. Remember Jacks outrank Queens.
strategy.intermediate: Create voids by discarding your only card of a suit on a trick your partner is winning. This lets you trump when that suit is led later. Track which high cards have been played.
strategy.advanced: Communication strategy: The stronger partner should take control, asking specific questions while revealing minimal information. Coordinate to capture opponent's high cards. The dealer's immediate scoring from the trump indicator can be decisive - if you turn up a 7 of trumps, you score 5 points instantly.
tips: Track Sevens and Aces - once played, you know the highest remaining card in each suit
The 10 tricks each contribute 1 bonus point - winning tricks matters even without high cards
Use communication wisely - don't give opponents more information than necessary
If you have multiple Sevens, you're in a very strong position

variations.name: Target score
variations.description: Common targets are 35 or 45 game points; sometimes 70 or 71 for a single long game. Match may be best of three games to 45, or first two to 35 then deciding game to 45.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Target score is a match-level option not yet mapped to engine constants.

variations.name: Exposure of cards when dealing
variations.description: Some play that dealer may expose the bottom card (trump) before dealing, and may expose cards from certain packets; tournament rules forbid exposure during the deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal exposure rules are procedural and not represented in engine overrides.

variations.name: Communication rules
variations.description: Local conventions vary: sometimes only the team currently winning the trick may speak; some require yes/no or numeric answers only; some allow concealing holding the mariglia of trumps when asked.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Communication conventions are table rules not modeled in engine.

scoring.description: Card points: 7=5, A=4, K=3, J=2, Q=1; 6-2=0. Each trick won adds 1 point. Team with more than 35 card points scores the difference as game points. First team to reach agreed target (commonly 35 or 45) wins the game.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach or exceed the agreed target score (35 or 45 game points) wins the game.
